content_html:
When planning your trip to Peru, one of the most important —and often overlooked— factors is the exchange rate. Understanding how it works can help you save money, avoid losses, and enjoy your travel experience even more.

In this article, we explain in a simple way how the exchange rate affects your trip and how to make the most of it.

Why is the exchange rate important?

The exchange rate is the value at which you can convert your currency (for example, US dollars or euros) into Peruvian soles (PEN), the official currency of the country.

What matters:
This value changes every day.

That means:

  • One day you may get more soles for your money
  • Another day, less

Small variations may seem insignificant, but throughout your trip they can represent noticeable savings—or extra expenses.

The exchange rate changes constantly

The exchange rate depends on global economic factors, which is why:

  • It changes daily
  • It may vary between cities like Lima and Cusco
  • It also differs between exchange houses, banks, and airports

For example:
Airports usually offer a less favorable exchange rate, meaning you will receive less money for your dollars or euros.

How to check the exchange rate before traveling

Before arriving in Peru, it’s recommended to check the current exchange rate. You can easily do this through:

  • Financial apps
  • Google (searching “USD to PEN”)
  • Bank or currency exchange websites

Practical tip:
Check the exchange rate a few days before your trip to have a reference and know whether you’re getting a good deal when exchanging money.

Real example: How much is $100 USD worth in Peru?

Let’s assume an approximate exchange rate:

1 USD = 3.70 PEN

Then:

$100 USD ≈ 370 Peruvian soles

What can you use that money for?

  • Several meals at local restaurants
  • Transportation within the city
  • Tickets to tourist attractions
  • Shopping in local markets

Now imagine the exchange rate drops to 3.50:
You would receive only 350 soles (20 soles less!)

This clearly shows how the exchange rate directly impacts your travel budget.

How to make the most of your money during your trip

To maximize your budget:

  • Exchange money at reliable exchange houses (better than airports or hotels)
  • Avoid exchanging large amounts all at once
  • Compare rates before making a decision
  • Carry a mix of cash and card

Travel better with planning

At GT Peru Travel, we help you plan every detail, including how to manage your money from the moment you arrive in the country.

Contact us for personalized advice and enjoy your trip without worries while discovering incredible destinations like Machu Picchu.
